texts.facts: Judgment: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of th e PFA Act and Rules. DA vs Madan Sharma 2. As per the complaint, on 23.07.2007, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Shri V.P.S. Chaudhary and FA Balwant Shah under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM) Shri K.K. Sharma visited the premises of M/s Kumar Milk Supplier, I-49, 50, Rama Park Road, Mohan Garden, New Delhi - 59, where accused Madan Sharma was found conducting business of various kind of milk and milk products including "Mixed Milk" for sale for human consumption, which was lying in an open tanki. The FI disclosed his identity and Da vs Madan Sharma on 11 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139798839/ 1 expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Mixed Milk" from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted of 1500 ml of "Mixed Milk" was taken from the tanki for analysis from the accused. The sample was taken under the supervision/ direction of Sh. K.K. Sharma SDM/LHA. The sample was taken after proper homogenization with the help of a measure already lying in the container by rotating it in all possible directions. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry glass bottles. 40 drops of formalin was added in each sample bottle. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice was given to accused Madan Sharma and the price of sample was also offered to him vide receipt dated 23.07.2007. Panchnama too was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by FI were signed by accused Madan Sharma and the other witness Sh. Balwant Shah FA. Before DA vs Madan Sharma starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh.Balwant Shah, FA was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA Code No. 91/LHA/19027 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the SDM/LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be non-confirming to standards. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample does not conform to standard because milk fat and milk solids not fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 4.5% and 8.5% respectively" 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Madan Sharma was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Kumar Milk Supplier, I-49, 50, Rama Park Road, Mohan Garden, New Delhi - 59 at the time of sampling and as such incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the Court on 12.11.2007 alleging violation of section 2 (ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act, 1954, which is punishable under Section 16(1A) read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 by the accused. DA vs Madan Sharma 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 12.11.2007. The accused thereafter exercised his option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. Based on the report of the CFL notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)&(m) Da vs Madan Sharma on 11 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139798839/ 2 of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case. PW-1 FI V.P.S. Chaudhary and PW-3 FA Balwant Shah were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh K.K. Sharma. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of "Mixed Milk" lying in an open tanki from the vendor for analysis, homogenization with the help of a measure already lying in the tanki, dividing it into three parts by putting in three clean and dry sample glass bottles, putting 40 drops of formalin in each sample bottle, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW- 1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C. Thereafter, on the next working day i.e. 24.07.2007, one counterpart of the sample alongwith copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII was deposited in intact condition with PA vide DA vs Madan Sharma receipt Ex.PW1/D and remaining two counterparts of the sample in intact condition alongwith two copies of Memos in Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E. Thereafter, PA Report Ex. PW-1/F was received according to which the sample does not conform to standards. During the investigation, PW-1 sent letter Ex.PW1/G to STO Ward No. 61 and received its reply stating that the firm ws not found registered with Sales Tax. During the investigation, vendor also furnished his statement Ex.PW1/H. Thereafter, on competition of investigation, the entire case file were sent through LHA to Director (PFA), who after going through the case file, applied his mind and gave his Consent for prosecution Ex.PW1/I against the accused. Thereafter the present complaint Ex. PW1/J was before this Court. Then intimation letter Ex. PW1/K alongwith copies of PA's Reports were sent to the accused through postal receipt Ex.PW1/L. These witnesses were duly cross- examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 04.03.2015 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter, the accused has not lead defence evidence and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 12. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 13. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed as under:- (a) The accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt if on account of delay or lapse on the part of prosecution to institute a prosecution, the Director CFL is unable to analyse the sample because of delay or of the sample undergoes a change for this reason. (b) Once the Director has examined the sample and has delivered his certificate, under proviso to sub-section (5) of section 13 of the Act, the certificate is final and conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein. 16. In this regard, the defence strongly relies upon the judgement titled as Kanshi Nath v. State [2005(2) FAC 219], informing that the said ruling has been constantly followed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in many other decisions. 17. This issue of variation was considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Delhi Administration vs Vidya Gupta Criminal Appeal No. 625 of 2018 dated 24.04.2018 wherein it was held that the finding of Hon'ble High Court in Kanshi Nath vs State and State vs Mahender Kumar & Ors, which hold that if in DA vs Madan Sharma the comparison of reports of PA and the Director vast variations are found, then the samples are not representative, is improper.
